notes: Twelve labels are printed, so twelve turns, six of them the chair with the identical label 'Sr. PRESIDENTE.-' and different opening words. The eleventh turn ('Se ha dejado constancia, señor senador.') is followed by two indented unlabelled paragraphs ('Ruego a los senadores...' and 'La Presidencia continuará pasando lista...'); by rule 2 I kept them inside that same turn rather than opening new ones — they read as the chair continuing. The chair is printed with no surname throughout, as the pre-2016 convention has it, and I recorded it that way. Every stenographer line here opens with a plain hyphen glued to the word ('-Se continúa llamando.') except the roll-call continuation, which prints a space and an ellipsis after the dash ('- ...Uzandizaga, Villarroel y Villaverde.') — I kept both exactly as printed. The attendance roll is split into two stenographer paragraphs, interrupted by the chair's turns, and I counted them as two separate events since they stand as separate paragraphs. The roll also contains a double space ('Alasino,  Avelín'). Typographic oddity worth flagging: inside the long roll paragraph, the single line 'Maya, Melgarejo, Meneghini, Menem, Moreau, O'Donnell, Oyarzún,' is rendered noticeably lighter and thinner than the lines above and below it, as if that one line carried a different font or weight. The signature of the Director del Cuerpo de Taquígrafos closes the provisional version; it is not speech, so I filed it as furniture. Below it roughly the bottom quarter of the page is blank.
